ordered_diagnoses: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder

s1.syndrome_frame: Hematuria and dysuria with a bladder lesion
salient_findings: Focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder
Heterogeneous enhancement of the lesion on CT
key_facts: Past medical history of abdominal hysterectomy
Urinalysis showed 6–8 red blood cells and 4–6 pus cells per high-power field
Ultrasound showed a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder
CT showed a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall
Lesion demonstrated heterogeneous enhancement on CT
Right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation

shortlist: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder

shortlist.label: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Most common type of bladder cancer, consistent with imaging findings of a polypoidal lesion in the bladder

shortlist.label: Papillary urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Specific type of transitional cell carcinoma, matches the description of a polypoidal lesion with heterogeneous enhancement on CT

shortlist.label: Bladder endometriosis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible cause of hematuria and dysuria in a woman with a history of abdominal hysterectomy, could be related to the bladder lesion

shortlist.label: Malacoplakia of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Rare condition that can cause bladder lesions and hematuria, consistent with the presence of calcific specks on CT

shortlist.label: Inverted papilloma of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Benign tumor that can cause hematuria and dysuria, could be a possible diagnosis given the polypoidal nature of the lesion

raw.rationale: The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder on ultrasound and a well-defined soft-tissue-density lesion with calcific specks along the anterosuperior bladder wall on CT, which demonstrated heterogeneous enhancement, are highly suggestive of a neoplastic process. Papillary urothelial carcinoma is a common type of bladder cancer that can present with these imaging findings.

rejected.label: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder
rejected.why: While this is a broad category that includes papillary urothelial carcinoma, the specific term 'papillary urothelial carcinoma' better describes the likely diagnosis based on the polypoidal nature of the lesion.

rejected.label: Bladder endometriosis
rejected.why: The imaging findings do not strongly support endometriosis, which would more likely present with cystic lesions or nodules in the bladder wall, often associated with the menstrual cycle.

rejected.label: Malacoplakia of the bladder
rejected.why: Malacoplakia typically presents with multiple small lesions or a single large mass, often with a history of chronic infection, which is not clearly indicated in this case.

rejected.label: Inverted papilloma of the bladder
rejected.why: Inverted papilloma is a rare, benign tumor that can mimic malignant lesions but typically does not show the heterogeneous enhancement seen on CT in this case.
